description: Construction of 2 x single family dwelling houses with private amenities.
decision_conditions: The proposed development, by reason of its scale, siting, layout and overall intensity of development, would result in the loss of a prominent open verge that contributes positively to the spacious and verdant character of the surrounding area. The proposed dwellings would be positioned significantly behind the established building line and would introduce a form of development that fails to respond positively to the prevailing pattern of development and urban grain of the locality. Furthermore, the extent of hardstanding, parking provision and associated development would materially erode the openness and corner plot character currently exhibited by the site. The proposal would therefore appear as an incongruous and overly intensive form of development that would cause harm to the character and appearance of the streetscene and surrounding area. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies D3 and D4 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD6, DMD8 and DMD37 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014), and the design objectives of the National Planning Policy Framework.

The proposed development, by reason of its siting, scale, massing and proximity to the common boundary with No.38 Capel Road, would result in an unduly dominant and overbearing form of development that would give rise to an unacceptable sense of enclosure and loss of outlook for neighbouring occupiers. Furthermore, insufficient information has been submitted to satisfactorily demonstrate that the development would not result in unacceptable impacts upon daylight and sunlight available to neighbouring residential properties. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies D3 and D4 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), and Policies DMD6, DMD8 and DMD10 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The proposed development, by virtue of the inadequate internal floor areas of both dwellings, would fail to meet the minimum internal space standards required by Policy D6 of the London Plan, resulting in a poor standard of residential accommodation for future occupiers. The proposal is therefore contrary to Chapter 12 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021), CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) DMD8 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The proposed development, by reason of the excessive level of vehicle parking proposed, would provide parking significantly in excess of the maximum standards set out in the London Plan. The resultant dominance of parking and hardstanding across the site frontage would undermine sustainable travel objectives and erode the landscaped corner plot character of the site to the detriment of the streetscene. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies T6 and T6.1 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP24 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and Policy DMD45 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The proposed development would require the formation of a substantial vehicular crossover serving multiple parking spaces in a position immediately adjacent to the junction of Capel Road. The siting of the access would result in an unsafe arrangement that would prejudice pedestrian and highway safety through increased vehicle movements and turning conflicts at the junction. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies T2 and T6 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP24 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), and Policies DMD45 and DMD47 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).
